title: Orchestrator timing race caused dual-canary serve and rollback failure
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Summary: During a scheduled canary promotion on 2026-03-09 we observed a short-lived period (~90s) where two canary variants were simultaneously serving traffic for a subset of routes and a subsequent automated rollback failed to converge due to version-pin state divergence. This ticket captures the incident timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and recommended long-term fixes and follow-ups.
impact_summary: Approximately 0.4% of requests experienced elevated latency (95th percentile increased from 120ms to 2.1s) and ~0.05% of requests observed mixed-model responses (inconsistent model versions). No customer data was exposed. A small number of enterprise tenants reported request errors (~20 tenants), triggering automated retries and some user-visible degradation for <5 minutes.
detection: On-call alerted via PagerDuty at 2026-03-09T14:07Z after the canary health dashboard crossed the alert threshold (error rate > 0.5% over 1 minute). SLO and trace sampling pointed to a narrow time window with elevated tail latency and mixed version identifiers in trace tags.
timeline:
- 14:00Z: Canary promotion job (operator-initiated) started.
- 14:03Z: Orchestrator change (route translator assign phase) began; concurrent autoscaler heartbeat caused an orchestrator leader re-election.
- 14:04Z: Two canary variants briefly existed in the routing table due to a timing window where weight update and pin state update were applied out-of-order.
- 14:05Z: Traffic split observed with 0.8% routed to both variants on some route shards.
- 14:06Z: Automated rollback triggered due to health signals but rollback attempted while a version-pin transaction was in-flight, leading to pin-state divergence across controllers.
- 14:07Z: On-call manual intervention applied temporary route lock and forced pin reconciliation; traffic returned to normal by 14:12Z.
- 14:20Z: Post-incident monitoring validated stable state.
root_cause: Race condition in the orchestrator sequence when handling concurrent control-plane events (promotion and autoscaler leader churn). The orchestrator applied route weight changes before the version-pin atomic commit completed, creating a window where routing allowed two canary binaries to serve. The rollback flow did not perform atomic compare-and-swap on pin-state, so conflicting controllers overrode each other and rollback failed to converge until manual reconciliation.
immediate_mitigation:
- Applied temporary ‘route-update’ global lock to prevent concurrent promotions while we patched controllers.
- Forced pin-state reconciliation script (internal tool) to canonicalize version pin across all controllers.
- Increased health-check sampling window to reduce sensitivity to short-lived spikes.
- Notified affected customers and disabled automated canary promotions for the day.
long_term_fixes:
- Implement atomic version-pin compare-and-swap in the orchestrator to guarantee single-writer semantics for pin state.
- Add a staged apply: ensure version-pin commit completes before any route weight application (strict two-phase commit pattern).
- Harden leader-election to avoid transient dual-leader windows impacting control-plane sequences.
- Add invariant checker that detects and alerts on dual-serving (two active variants for same route) within 10s and auto-evicts the older variant until human review.
- Extend rollout acceptance tests to cover concurrent autoscaler events and leader churn scenarios.
- Add canary smoke test that validates route/pin consistency before cutover traffic is allowed.
action_items: ENG-86001: Implement atomic compare-and-swap for version-pin in orchestrator (owner: Tomas Li, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-27)
ENG-86002: Add route-lock mechanism and abort-on-concurrent-policy (owner: Priya Kapoor, estimate: 2, due: 2026-03-24)
ENG-86003: Leader-election hardening and tests for transient churn (owner: Mei Chen, estimate: 5, due: 2026-04-03)
ENG-86004: Invariant detector and dual-serve auto-evict tool (owner: Jordan Park, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-31)
ENG-86005: Rollout test harness update to simulate concurrent autoscaler events (owner: SRE Team, estimate: 4, due: 2026-04-07)
DOC-370: Runbook update: add forced-pin-reconcile procedure and checklist (owner: Aisha Raman, estimate: 1, due: 2026-03-18)
ENG-86006: Post-deploy health-check tuning rollback policy (owner: DevEx, estimate: 2, due: 2026-03-22)
follow_ups: Ensure canary promotions are gated by the new acceptability smoke tests (tracked in ENG-86005).
Coordinate with Customer Success to follow up with any tenants that opened tickets during the window; collect any additional traces.
Schedule a post-implementation validation blitz (1 hour) after fixes land to exercise leader churn and verify invariants.
postmortem_notes: Trade-offs considered: we evaluated a fast-fail approach that would abort promotions on any concurrent control-plane event but rejected it due to increased operational friction for high-frequency rollouts. Instead we opted for targeted atomicity on version pins and a short (5s) route-apply hold to preserve rollout velocity. Review feedback from PM and SRE recommended additional observability which has been incorporated into action items.
